note:
Round 3 for /pages/pdrn-research `key_findings` block `f2`. R2 delivered both of Malcolm's changes — the granules enlarge and glow at each arrival, the strands mend and thicken and glow, and every pearl blob is gone from both layers. It also introduced one fault, and the fault is a direct consequence of the change.

### 'MEND BROKEN STRANDS' AND 'NO HOLLOW TUBE ENDS' ARE IN TENSION, AND NOTHING IN THE BRIEF RESOLVED IT

A break has ends. Every engine in this family draws the end of a fibre as a CUT PIPE — an elliptical open bore with a visible dark interior. Confirmed at native pixels on the best r2 frame, `pdrn-r2-edit--A-two-changes-nbp_flash_01`, where three broken strands on the left show open mouths.

That exact fault is on this project's record twice over: `block-firming-peptide-approach.json` names it as the thing that killed a candidate ('HOLLOW TUBE ENDS, the open-bore fault... any fibre end in shot must be solid'), and it is negated by name in both the r1 and r2 negative lists. Negating it did not work, because a negative cannot answer a question the brief creates: r2 ASKED for gaps and said nothing about what the ends of a gap look like. A negative removes; only a description decides. Same lesson as [[describe-the-thing-dont-name-it]] — the brief named 'gaps' and let every engine fill in the ends its own way.

So r3 DESCRIBES THE ENDS. A broken strand ends the way a snapped cord ends: SOLID all the way through, ROUNDED and CLOSED OFF, with no opening, no rim, no dark interior and no visible wall thickness. The fibres are solid rods, not tubes, and a break exposes solid material.

NOTHING ELSE CHANGES FROM R2. The two changes Malcolm asked for are already right and are restated verbatim so an edit does not undo them. The comb-versus-ladder fix and the warmth nudge also carry forward.

TWO ROUTES AGAIN, and this time the second one is the cheap surgical option:
  fromr1  edit from the ORIGINAL chosen frame, the full r2 instruction plus the solid-ends description. Gives
          several fresh candidates.
  fromr2  edit from the best r2 frame itself, changing ONLY the broken ends. Least likely to disturb anything
          that is already correct, most likely to be a one-line fix — and most at risk of an edit redrawing
          more than it was asked to, which is why both are run and compared.

FLUX.2 stays excluded on r1 evidence (no spheres, no shafts, no arrival on either concept). Luma ignores references in this runner, so it is absent from both edit routes.

CHECK AT NATIVE PIXELS, ON THE FIBRE BAND SPECIFICALLY: every strand end in shot solid and closed; the granule enlargement still slight and still local; no pearl blob anywhere in either layer; the fibre state still one continuous gradient rather than two halves.

slots.title: from the original pick · both changes plus solid closed strand ends
slots.prompt:
Keep this illustration exactly as it is — the same camera square on to the cut face, the same block of skin filling the same part of the frame, the same layer order, the same clear glass spheres floating above in the same positions, the same slender shafts of warm white light descending from them, the same pale hazy background, the same soft glossy style. Change only what is described below, and warm the whole picture slightly so the tissue reads as a soft warm peach-cream rather than a cool grey-pink.

FIRST, REMOVE EVERY SMOOTH PEARL-WHITE BLOB THAT SITS INSIDE THE TISSUE. In the band of small round granules there must be no large egg-shaped pearl body and no cupped or dish-shaped object. Deep among the fibre bundles there must be no rounded pearl cell of any kind. Everywhere one of those blobs used to be, there is simply more of the layer it was sitting in.

SECOND, IN THE BAND OF SMALL ROUND GRANULES, the arriving light acts on the granules themselves. Where each shaft reaches that band, the small round granules already there are SLIGHTLY LARGER than their neighbours — a little plumper and rounder, only a little — and they GLOW SOFTLY FROM WITHIN with a warm light, brightest right where the light arrives and easing back smoothly with distance, so that toward the sides of the block the granules are their ordinary smaller size and unlit. The change is gradual, with no line and no edge.

THIRD, IN THE DEEP ZONE OF LONG FIBRE BUNDLES, the arriving light acts on the fibres themselves. Toward the left and right sides of the block, away from any shaft, some bundles are THIN and slack and a few are INTERRUPTED BY SHORT GAPS. Where a shaft reaches the fibre zone, those same strands are WHOLE AND CONTINUOUS, noticeably THICKER and fuller, and GLOWING SOFTLY FROM WITHIN, with fine bright filaments bridging across where the gaps were and closing them. The change from one state to the other is a smooth gradient across the block, never an abrupt division and never two halves.

FOURTH, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: EVERY STRAND IS A SOLID ROD, NOT A TUBE. Where a strand is interrupted, its two ends are SOLID ALL THE WAY THROUGH and SMOOTHLY ROUNDED OFF, closed like the end of a snapped cord or a broken stick of chalk. No end has an opening, a hole, a dark interior, a rim, a ring or any visible wall thickness. Nothing anywhere in the fibre layer may look like a cut pipe, a straw or a piece of tubing seen end-on. Every end in the picture is filled, solid and rounded.

FIFTH, INSIDE THE GLASS SPHERES, the small flat pearl ladders must be drawn properly: TWO PARALLEL ROWS OF PEARL BEADS, one along the top and one along the bottom, BOTH RUNNING THE FULL LENGTH, joined by short fine crossbars, with the ends closed. Not a comb, a fork or a rake with teeth along one side. They stay flat and face-on, straight and level, never curled and never twisted. Spheres holding loose scattered single beads keep them exactly as they are.

Nothing else changes. No object is added and none of the layers change place.
